summary_paragraph: A man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, COPD, and alcohol dependence was re-admitted for worsening shortness of breath and volume overload due to medication non-compliance and heavy alcohol use. He presented with dyspnea, abdominal swelling, and cough, and was found to have elevated proBNP, mild pulmonary congestion on chest X-ray, and signs of fluid retention. He received IV furosemide and was monitored for alcohol withdrawal. An ultrasound showed an echogenic liver and splenomegaly, raising concern for early cirrhosis. Despite medical advice, he left against medical advice on hospital day two, still volume overloaded. He was discharged on his baseline heart failure medications with strong counseling to adhere to treatment and avoid alcohol.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, continuous
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Nonspecific elevation of levels of transaminase or lactic acid dehydrogenase [LDH]
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
